title: Open Science and Research Integrity
fullTitle: IELTS Hourly Practice — Science, Research, Space, and Archaeology: Open Science and Research Integrity
angle: Building trustworthy science through replication, transparency, and balanced public funding

sections.title: Reading
sections.html:
Scientific progress rarely moves directly from discovery to public benefit. A promising result may fail during replication, prove too expensive to scale, or create ethical concerns that were invisible in the laboratory. Strong research systems therefore reward not only original ideas but also verification, transparent reporting, and collaboration. Open science is one response. Researchers share methods, data, and sometimes early findings so that other specialists can examine them. This can expose errors sooner and reduce duplicated effort. Yet openness also creates risks. Sensitive medical data require protection, and preliminary results may be misunderstood when reported without context. Universities need rules that balance transparency, privacy, and accuracy. Funding design matters as well. Short grants can generate quick outputs, but they may discourage difficult projects whose value appears only after many years. Unlimited support without milestones can also waste public money. A balanced model combines stable core funding with periodic review, independent peer assessment, and room for high-risk investigation. Scientific reliability ultimately depends on institutions as much as on talented individuals. When integrity, replication, and long-term learning are valued, societies are more likely to convert uncertain discoveries into trustworthy knowledge and practical innovation.

Khoa học đáng tin cậy cần tái lập, minh bạch, tài trợ cân bằng và thể chế mạnh.

1. Name two reasons a discovery may not create public benefit. 2. What does open science share? 3. What privacy risk is mentioned? 4. Why can short grants be harmful? 5. What supports reliable science?

Trả lời năm câu hỏi theo bài đọc.

1. Replication, cost, or ethics. 2. Methods, data, and early findings. 3. Exposure of sensitive medical data. 4. They discourage long-term projects. 5. Institutions valuing integrity and verification.

Đáp án có giải thích ngắn gọn.

sections.title: Listening
sections.html:
Host: Our university plans a citizen-science air-quality project.

Người dẫn: Trường đại học lên kế hoạch dự án chất lượng không khí.

Dr. Lee: Volunteers will carry low-cost sensors during daily journeys and upload readings each evening.

Tiến sĩ Lee: Tình nguyện viên mang cảm biến và tải dữ liệu lên mỗi tối.

Host: Will these devices replace official stations?

Người dẫn: Chúng có thay thế trạm chính thức không?

Dr. Lee: No. They supplement the network; that word is important. Official stations remain the reference.

Tiến sĩ Lee: Không. Chúng chỉ bổ sung mạng lưới.

Host: What is the main challenge?

Người dẫn: Thách thức chính là gì?

Dr. Lee: Calibration. Cheap sensors can drift, so each device must be checked before and after field use. Weather can also distort readings, so our software will flag unusual values instead of deleting them automatically.

Tiến sĩ Lee: Hiệu chuẩn là thách thức; thời tiết cũng có thể làm sai lệch dữ liệu.

Host: Will volunteers receive personal medical advice?

Người dẫn: Họ có nhận tư vấn y tế cá nhân không?

Dr. Lee: No. We will show neighborhood patterns because the sensors cannot diagnose individual exposure accurately.

Tiến sĩ Lee: Không, chỉ có xu hướng theo khu vực.

1. What will volunteers carry? 2. Do sensors replace stations? 3. What is the main challenge? 4. When are devices checked? 5. What results are shared?

Trả lời năm câu hỏi.

1. Low-cost sensors. 2. No, they supplement them. 3. Calibration. 4. Before and after field use. 5. Neighborhood patterns.

Bẫy: replace khác supplement.

sections.title: Writing (Task 2)
sections.html:
Some people believe governments should concentrate research funding on projects that produce immediate practical benefits. Others think basic research should receive equal or greater support. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

Một số người cho rằng chính phủ nên tập trung kinh phí nghiên cứu vào các dự án tạo lợi ích thực tiễn ngay lập tức, trong khi người khác cho rằng nghiên cứu cơ bản cần được hỗ trợ ngang bằng hoặc nhiều hơn.

Governments face constant pressure to ensure that public money produces visible results. This explains why some people favor research with immediate practical benefits, while others argue that basic science deserves equal or greater support. In my view, public funding should maintain a deliberate balance, because short-term problem solving and long-term discovery serve different but complementary purposes. Supporters of applied research reasonably point to urgent social needs. Investment in vaccines, clean-energy systems, agricultural technology, or safer infrastructure can improve lives within a measurable period. Such projects are also easier to evaluate because policymakers can track outcomes such as reduced emissions, lower treatment costs, or higher productivity. When budgets are tight, directing funds toward clearly defined problems may therefore appear both responsible and efficient. However, an exclusive focus on immediate usefulness would be shortsighted. Many transformative technologies emerged from research that initially had no obvious commercial purpose. Basic studies of electricity, genetics, and computing created knowledge that later supported entire industries. Moreover, scientists cannot always predict which discovery will become valuable. If funding agencies demand near-term applications from every proposal, researchers may avoid ambitious questions and concentrate on safer, incremental work. A balanced funding model is consequently preferable. Governments should reserve substantial resources for mission-driven projects addressing urgent priorities, while also protecting long-term grants for investigator-led basic research. Both streams should be assessed through rigorous peer review, transparent milestones, and periodic evaluation rather than simplistic promises of instant impact. In conclusion, practical research offers clear public value, but basic science provides the intellectual foundation from which future solutions emerge. Governments should not choose one at the expense of the other; they should design a portfolio that meets present needs while preserving the capacity for unexpected discovery.

Bài mẫu lập luận rằng nghiên cứu ứng dụng và nghiên cứu cơ bản có vai trò bổ sung cho nhau.

Structure: introduction, immediate-benefit case, basic-research case, balanced policy, conclusion.

Cấu trúc: mở bài, lợi ích ngắn hạn, nghiên cứu cơ bản, chính sách cân bằng, kết luận.

Improvement 1: Use precise examples rather than listing many sectors.

Cải thiện 1: Dùng ví dụ chính xác.

Improvement 2: Contrast measurable impact with uncertain long-term value.

Cải thiện 2: Đối chiếu tác động đo lường được với giá trị dài hạn.

Improvement 3: State a workable funding mechanism.

Cải thiện 3: Nêu cơ chế tài trợ có thể triển khai.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.html:
Part 1: Do you enjoy reading about science?

Bạn có thích đọc về khoa học không?

Yes, especially when discoveries connect to daily life.

Có, nhất là khi khám phá liên quan đến đời sống.

Part 1: Should schools teach practical science?

Trường học có nên dạy khoa học thực hành?

Yes, because experiments show how evidence is produced.

Có, vì thí nghiệm cho thấy bằng chứng được tạo ra thế nào.

Describe a scientific discovery or research project that you find interesting. Say what it is, how you learned about it, why it matters, and what questions remain.

Mô tả một khám phá hoặc dự án khoa học thú vị.

Prepare: discovery, source, value, open questions.

I find mRNA vaccine research particularly interesting. I learned about it during the COVID-19 pandemic, when reports explained that scientists could use genetic instructions to train the immune system. What impressed me most was that the underlying work had continued for decades before producing a widely used medical product. This shows why basic science matters even when its immediate value is unclear. The technology may shorten vaccine design because researchers can identify a relevant sequence and create a targeted instruction rather than grow a weakened virus. However, development still requires safety testing, manufacturing, storage, and clear public communication. The research also raises unresolved questions. Scientists need to understand how long protection lasts, how formulations can be stored more easily, and how access can be made fair across countries. There are communication problems too, because uncertainty is sometimes presented as evidence that science is unreliable. I admire this field because it combines biology, engineering, public health, and ethics. It demonstrates that discovery alone is not enough; trustworthy institutions are needed to translate knowledge into a safe and useful product.

Bài mẫu về công nghệ vaccine mRNA.

Part 3: Should scientists control public research budgets?

Nhà khoa học có nên kiểm soát ngân sách nghiên cứu?

They need strong influence, but elected bodies and citizens should also shape priorities.

Họ cần ảnh hưởng lớn, nhưng chính phủ và công chúng cũng phải tham gia.

Part 3: Why is science sometimes distrusted?

Vì sao khoa học đôi khi bị nghi ngờ?

Poor communication, conflicting early studies, polarization, and past failures can reduce trust.

Truyền thông kém, nghiên cứu mâu thuẫn, phân cực và thất bại trước đây làm giảm niềm tin.

sections.title: Strategy Note
sections.html:
For science topics, distinguish evidence, interpretation, and policy choice.

Với chủ đề khoa học, hãy phân biệt bằng chứng, cách diễn giải và lựa chọn chính sách.

In Writing Task 2, avoid claiming that one study proves a universal conclusion.

Trong Writing Task 2, tránh khẳng định một nghiên cứu chứng minh kết luận phổ quát.

In Speaking, explain one mechanism clearly before adding examples.

Trong Speaking, giải thích rõ một cơ chế trước khi thêm ví dụ.
